note: The OLG's 'Household Ineligibility for TBA' section on the TBA Overview page lists three ineligibility criteria: (1) non-compliance with a TAFDC program requirement, (2) non-compliance with a SNAP work requirement, and (3) disqualification due to IPV. This partially maps to FNS 727.1's four criteria. FNS criterion #1 (lost TANF/SFCA due to sanction) is arguably covered by the OLG's 'has not complied with a TAFDC program requirement,' though the OLG uses broader language rather than specifically referencing sanctions. FNS criterion #2 (disqualified from SNAP) is covered by the OLG's IPV disqualification item, though the OLG is narrower — it specifies only IPV disqualification, while FNS says 'disqualified from SNAP' which could include other disqualification types. FNS criterion #3 (household receiving TANF/SFCA again) is NOT addressed in the OLG's ineligibility list. The Reclassification page notes that reinstated TAFDC cases revert to PA status, but this doesn't explicitly state that receiving TAFDC again ends TBA eligibility. FNS criterion #4 (state-designated ineligible categories) is not addressed — Massachusetts may not have designated any such categories, but this is not documented. The OLG also adds a criterion not in FNS: non-compliance with SNAP work requirements. The QC-specific procedural requirements in FNS 727.1 (using standard vs. transitional review procedures) are not applicable to the OLG as they pertain to QC reviewer methodology.
